## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Parivattanahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying a Reversal: Analysis") constitutes the twelfth division (Ne 12) of the *Nettippakaraṇa* [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship, Giuliana Martini cites Ne 12 (occurring at PTS Nett 65) for its exposition of the two types of reliance or dependence (*nissaya*): reliance on craving (*taṇhānissaya*) and reliance on views (*diṭṭhinissaya*) [Martini]. The passage analyzes how intentions conditioned by attachment or delusion act as volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*) that give rise to the full sequence of dependent arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) [Martini].

Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus shows extensive sharing of canonical material, identifying 320 matching passages between Ne 12 and 14 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The text's most substantial reuse connections are with the *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the sub-commentary *Nettivibhāvinī*, the *Mahācattārīsaka Sutta* (MN 117), and the *Dasuttara Sutta* (DN 34), along with the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and chapter 8 (*Hārasampātabhūmi*) of the *Peṭakopadesa* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns sections of Ne 12 with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), Sanskrit treatises including the *Yogācārabhūmi* and *Ādikarmapradīpa*, and a Tibetan Mahāyāna translation (*Ārya-bodhisattvagocara-upāyaviṣayavikurvāṇanirdeśa-sūtra*, D 146) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
